title: DevOps checks
bridge: The DevOps checks are like the lint and type steps in frontend-ci, moved to the infrastructure and gitops repos. Except: the most useful answer there is a plan or a rendered diff of real infrastructure. So CI gets a read-only role, and no workflow may ever apply, destroy or sync.
intro: Agents will propose infrastructure changes, and today infrastructure CI only checks formatting while gitops has no checks at all. This lesson adds six checks: validate, tflint and trivy; chart rendering; workflow lint; a read-only role; PR plans; and Argo CD diffs. They are YAML and HCL in the DevOps repos; nothing here is Python.

sections.h: Keyless checks, part 1: validate every module (G7-17)
p: Today the infrastructure repo runs one workflow, terrugrunt-lint.yml (spelled that way), which checks formatting only. Plans are run by hand over VPN and pasted into PRs. G7-17 adds .github/workflows/terraform-checks.yml next to it, with the same pattern. That means the same push paths, infrastructure-runner-set, actions pinned by SHA, and tenv (a version manager) to install OpenTofu.

tofu validate checks that a module's HCL is consistent: types, references, required arguments. With init -backend=false it needs no state and no credentials. Terragrunt units are covered later by plans (G7-32).
sections.because: We keep going after a failed module, because one report with all broken modules beats one fix per push.

code.text:
name: "[TERRAFORM] Checks"
on:
  push:
    paths: ['.github/workflows/terraform-checks.yml', 'terraform/**', 'modules/**', 'multi_tenant/**', 'single_tenant/**']
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  validate:
    name: Validate modules
    runs-on: infrastructure-runner-set
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
      - name: Install Tofu
        env:
          TENV_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: tenv tofu install
      - name: tofu validate every module (no backend, no cloud keys)
        run: |
          status=0
          for dir in modules/*/; do
            (cd "$dir" && tofu init -backend=false -input=false -no-color >/dev/null && tofu validate -no-color) \
              || { echo "::error file=${dir}::tofu validate failed"; status=1; }
          done
          exit $status

sections.h: Keyless checks, part 2: tflint and trivy
p: tflint finds mistakes validate cannot see, such as an instance type that does not exist. Add .tflint.hcl at the repo root with the aws and google rulesets. trivy config scans Terraform for risky settings, such as an open security group.

trivy runs with --severity HIGH,CRITICAL over modules/, terraform/ and multi_tenant/, advisory (exit code 0) for 2 weeks. Then go through the findings with Security, and fail on new HIGH and CRITICAL findings. Every line in .trivyignore names an owner and a reason. Fix or ignore the first-run errors in the same PR and list every ignored rule in the PR description.
sections.because: We pass GITHUB_TOKEN to tflint, because tflint --init downloads its rulesets from GitHub and would be rate-limited without it.

code.text:
tflint:
    name: tflint
    runs-on: infrastructure-runner-set
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
      - uses: terraform-linters/setup-tflint@<sha> # pin by SHA like the checkout above
      - run: tflint --init && tflint --recursive --config "$PWD/.tflint.hcl" --minimum-failure-severity=error
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  # trivy: aquasecurity/trivy-action@<sha> with scan-type: config, severity: HIGH,CRITICAL, exit-code: '0' for 2 weeks

callout.text: Ask for terraform-checks.yml, .tflint.hcl and .trivyignore to be protected paths (G0/G3 walls). An agent cannot loosen the checks that judge its infra PRs.

p: gitops has no checks today. A typo in a values file reaches Argo CD as a sync error on a real cluster. G7-23 renders every environment of each changed chart and checks the result against the Kubernetes schemas. It takes about a minute and needs no cluster access.

kubeconform validates Kubernetes YAML against the API schemas, offline. Custom resources (ExternalSecret, KEDA ScaledObject, HTTPRoute, Argo CD Application) take their schemas from the datreeio CRDs-catalog.
sections.because: We install a pinned kubeconform into a temp folder, because the runner image lacks it.

code.text:
name: Chart checks
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

permissions: { contents: read }

jobs:
  charts:
    runs-on: gitops-runner-set
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@<sha> # pin by SHA
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - uses: azure/setup-helm@<sha> # pin by SHA
      - name: Install kubeconform
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin" && echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          curl -sSL https://github.com/yannh/kubeconform/releases/download/v0.7.0/kubeconform-linux-amd64.tar.gz | tar xz -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin"

sections.h: Charts, part 2: lint and render every environment
p: A changed chart is a folder with a Chart.yaml that the PR touches, such as cloud/rhino-server or frontend/dashboard. For each one: helm dependency build (Chart.lock is committed, *.tgz is ignored), then helm lint. Then helm template for every <env>-values.yaml, piped into kubeconform -strict -summary. Use Nexus's helm proxy if a public chart repo rate-limits.
On the first run, list the current failures per environment in the PR and fix the cheap ones. Skip the rest with a comment and an owner.
sections.because: We render every values file, not only the default, because a typo in prod-aws-values.yaml breaks only prod.

code.text:
- name: Lint and render every environment of each changed chart
        run: |
          status=0
          charts=$(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | xargs -r -n1 dirname | sort -u \
            | while read -r d; do while [ "$d" != . ] && [ ! -f "$d/Chart.yaml" ]; do d=$(dirname "$d"); done; [ -f "$d/Chart.yaml" ] && echo "$d"; done | sort -u)
          for chart in $charts; do
            helm dependency build "$chart" >/dev/null && helm lint "$chart" || status=1
            for values in "$chart"/*-values.yaml; do
              [ -e "$values" ] || continue
              helm template ci "$chart" -f "$values" | kubeconform -strict -summary -kubernetes-version 1.36.0 \
                -schema-location default \
                -schema-location 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datreeio/CRDs-catalog/main/{{.Group}}/{{.ResourceKind}}_{{.ResourceAPIVersion}}.json' \
                || { echo "::error file=$values::does not render to valid manifests"; status=1; }
            done
          done
          exit $status

notes.text: One step does it all.
Collect failures; do not stop at the first.
Every changed file's folder ...
... walked up until a folder with Chart.yaml is found; that is the chart.
For each changed chart ...
... fetch its dependencies, then lint it.
For each environment's values file ...
... skipping when the glob matched nothing.
Render the manifests and pipe them into kubeconform. Use the oldest product cluster's Kubernetes version here.

... and the CRDs-catalog for custom resources.

Fail if any chart or environment failed.

callout.text: The G7-23 sketch hard-codes --kubernetes-version 1.36.0. Use the Kubernetes version of the oldest product cluster instead, so a chart that only works on a newer cluster fails here. Ask DevOps for that version and keep it in one variable.

p: Workflows hold CI tokens and OIDC roles, and agents will open PRs that touch them. actionlint catches broken workflows. zizmor catches risky ones: template injection, unpinned actions, wide permissions. Template injection is a ${{ }} expression with outside text inside a run: script. That text can then run as shell (lesson p2-3).

One small workflow is copied into fcp, infrastructure, gitops, byte, ai-agents and claude-plugins. Each repo's .github/actionlint.yaml lists its runner labels; add one to gitops with gitops-runner-set. fcp pins actions by tag, so its .github/zizmor.yml allows tags for actions/* and asks for SHAs everywhere else. Look first at comment-triggered workflows such as byte-review.yml: they run on untrusted input.
sections.because: We start zizmor advisory, because the first run will find old problems that need owners before the check may block.

code.text:
name: Workflow lint
on:
  push:
    paths: ['.github/workflows/**', '.github/actionlint.yaml', '.github/zizmor.yml']

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  lint:
    # fcp-runner-set here; infrastructure-runner-set, gitops-runner-set, ... in the other repos
    runs-on: fcp-runner-set
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6  # fcp pins by tag; infrastructure pins by SHA (keep each repo's style)
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: actionlint (runner labels come from .github/actionlint.yaml)
        run: uvx --from "actionlint-py==<pinned>" actionlint -color
      - name: zizmor (advisory for now)
        # .github/zizmor.yml: rules.unpinned-uses.config.policies: { "actions/*": ref-pin, "*": hash-pin }
        run: uvx "zizmor==<pinned>" --min-severity medium --config .github/zizmor.yml .github/workflows || true

sections.h: A read-only role for plans, part 1 (G7-30)
p: A plan needs to read the cloud, so it needs credentials. G7-30 creates a role that can read and do nothing else. In each AWS account, TerraformPlanRole lives in a new tree, terraform/accounts/<account>/aws/global/iam/terraform-plan/. Its template is the solutions account's github-actions folder.

Only one principal may assume it: the OIDC role GitHubActionsTerraformPlan in inf (123456789012). That role trusts only repo:RhinoHealth/infrastructure:pull_request, never repo:RhinoHealth/*. It can read the state bucket rhinohealth-terraform-state and assume each account's TerraformPlanRole.
sections.because: We name one exact principal in the trust policy, because any wider trust would let other repos or events read every account.

sections.h: A read-only role for plans, part 2: no data
p: ReadOnlyAccess alone could read S3 objects, secrets and table rows. A plan needs configuration, never data, so the role gets an explicit deny. In IAM an explicit deny beats any allow. Units whose data sources read secrets are skipped in PR plans.

Two more changes outside this file. account.hcl makes the role switchable: assume_role_arn = "arn:aws:iam::<id>:role/${get_env("TG_ROLE_NAME", "TerraformDeploymentRole")}". Plans also need a read-only Vault role terraform-plan (after G0 narrows gha-runners) and an EKS access entry with AmazonEKSViewPolicy. Until then, PR plans skip the units that need them.
sections.because: We deny data reads explicitly, because a plan job that can read secrets is one injected step away from leaking them.

p: The workflow is named "[TERRAGRUNT] Plan on PRs (read-only)" and runs on pull_request when files under terraform/, modules/, multi_tenant/ or single_tenant/ change. The block below is the rest of the file, from permissions down.

Units are the folders with a changed terragrunt.hcl. For a module-only change, add the units that use the module with Terragrunt 1.1's include-units-reading option; check its exact flag name. Never write plan files with -out: a plan file holds secret values in plain text. The comment script posts one sticky comment, edited on each push, with each unit's Plan line and changed addresses. The full output stays in the job log of this private repo.
sections.because: We plan with -lock=false, because the read-only role cannot write the lock file and a plan must never block a real apply.

code.text:
permissions: { id-token: write, contents: read, pull-requests: write }

jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: infrastructure-runner-set
    env:
      TG_ROLE_NAME: TerraformPlanRole  # read by account.hcl (G7-30); never TerraformDeploymentRole here
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@<sha> # pin by SHA
        with: { aws-region: us-east-1, role-to-assume: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/GitHubActionsTerraformPlan" }
      - name: Install Tofu and Terragrunt
        env: { TENV_GITHUB_TOKEN: "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" }
        run: tenv tofu install && tenv tg install
      - name: Plan the changed units (read-only, no lock, no plan files)
        run: |
          git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | grep 'terragrunt.hcl$' | xargs -r -n1 dirname | sort -u > units.txt
          # Module-only changes: add the units that read the module (Terragrunt 1.1 include-units-reading; check the flag).
          while read -r unit; do
            (cd "$unit" && terragrunt plan -lock=false -input=false -no-color) > "plan-${unit//\//_}.txt" 2>&1 || true
          done < units.txt
      - name: One comment with the summary per unit
        env: { GH_TOKEN: "${{ github.token }}" }
        run: .github/scripts/post_plan_comment.sh units.txt  # "Plan: X to add, Y to change, Z to destroy" + addresses

sections.h: Argo CD diffs on a throw-away cluster (G7-34)
p: The workflow is named "Argo CD diff preview", runs on pull_request to main, and has permissions contents: read and pull-requests: write. A values change can touch many environments at once, and reviewers cannot see that in the diff. argocd-diff-preview renders the Applications for main and for the PR on a throw-away kind cluster and posts the rendered manifest diff.

kind runs Kubernetes inside Docker; here it runs inside the runner pod's dind sidecar and dies with the pod. argocd/argocd-apps is a Helm chart installed with helm on inf. So there are no plain Application files for the tool to find, and the job renders them first. Every destination is a remote product cluster; the tool renders locally and never contacts them. Give it a read-only token for gitops and no cluster credentials at all.
sections.because: We check out main and the PR side by side, because the tool needs both rendered trees to compute the diff.

code.text:
diff:
    runs-on: gitops-runner-set  # ARC dind: kind runs inside the dind sidecar; nothing reaches a real cluster
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@<sha> # pin by SHA
        with: { path: pull-request }
      - uses: actions/checkout@<sha>
        with: { ref: main, path: main }
      - name: Render the Applications (argocd-apps is a Helm chart installed with helm on inf, not plain YAML)
        run: |
          for side in main pull-request; do
            for values in "$side"/argocd/argocd-apps/*-values.yaml; do
              helm template apps "$side/argocd/argocd-apps" -f "$values" > "$side/rendered-apps-$(basename "$values")"
            done
          done
      - name: Diff on a throw-away kind cluster
        run: |
          docker run --network host -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
            -v "$PWD/main:/base-branch" -v "$PWD/pull-request:/target-branch" -v "$PWD/output:/output" \
            -e TARGET_BRANCH="${{ github.head_ref }}" -e REPO="${{ github.repository }}" \
            dagandersen/argocd-diff-preview:<pinned version>
      - name: Post the diff
        env: { GH_TOKEN: "${{ github.token }}" }
        run: |
          gh pr comment "${{ github.event.number }}" --edit-last --body-file output/diff.md \
            || gh pr comment "${{ github.event.number }}" --body-file output/diff.md

quiz.q: Why does the plan workflow run terragrunt plan with -lock=false?

options.text: Because locks slow the plan down.
Because the read-only role cannot write the lock file, and a plan must never block a real apply.
options.why: use_lockfile writes a .tflock, which the role is not allowed to write.

options.text: Because Terragrunt ignores locks on pull requests.
options.why: It does not; the flag is our choice.

quiz.q: TerraformPlanRole has ReadOnlyAccess. Why add an explicit deny on s3:GetObject and secretsmanager:GetSecretValue?

options.text: ReadOnlyAccess could read objects and secret values, and a plan needs configuration only.
options.why: An explicit deny wins over the allow, so the role reads configuration and no data.

options.text: Because ReadOnlyAccess does not include S3.
options.why: It does include object reads; that is the problem.

options.text: To make the plan run faster.
options.why: It changes what the role may read, not speed.

quiz.q: An agent PR changes a gitops values file. What can the Argo CD diff workflow do?

options.text: Sync the change to a staging cluster to test it.
options.why: No argocd sync anywhere; nothing reaches a real cluster.

options.text: Apply it if the diff is small.
options.why: Applying and syncing stay a person's job.

options.text: Render main and the PR on a throw-away kind cluster and post the manifest diff.
options.why: It renders locally in the dind sidecar and only comments.
